neighbours.label: ' leaving' (and ' left') for what remains after something is removed ('remove the cells, leaving only the skeleton', 'leaving a thin crust'); 'leave/left' as departing or as a direction stays low.
fire: Boil the syrup down, leaving only a thick glaze.

Strip the bark, leaving the smooth wood underneath.
The fire burned the roof, leaving only the walls.
Drain the pasta, leaving a little water in the pot.
Erosion removed the soft rock, leaving tall pillars.
Scrape off the old paint, leaving clean metal.
The tide went out, leaving pools among the rocks.
quiet: Boil the syrup for ten minutes before serving.
The flood reached the town at dawn.
Strip the bed and wash the sheets.
The fire started in the kitchen.
She was leaving the office when it rained.
Turn left after the old mill.
The train is leaving from platform two.
